structured.reason: The "Tip for a Secure Fit" section implies a known weakness. It says "For a steadier hold, attach the frame to your mask with double-sided tape or thread." That reacts to reviews saying the bracket "won't stay in place," "is difficult to keep in place," and "keeps falling." It implies the product is not steady without extra effort, which is category 4 (conditional praise implying failure without special effort) and category 3 (defensive framing of a raised complaint). A secondary example is "Extra space in front of your mouth means less pressure against your lips, so talking and breathing feel more comfortable." This answers the reviewer complaints that the product made talking impossible and was uncomfortable. It is a plain positive claim, so it is weaker evidence on its own, but it points the same way. The rest of the description (specs, washability, lipstick protection, pack sizes) is neutral or positive.
